title: Venezuela’s Reconciliation Talks Continued Progress Toward an Enduring Democracy
summary_raw:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
November 24, 2026

The United States welcomes the conclusion of the latest round of political reconciliation talks between Venezuela’s 2015 National Assembly, led by Dr. Dinorah Figuera, and the interim government.  This Venezuelan-led process continues to advance the institutional reforms and political freedoms necessary for free, fair, and credible elections following Operation Absolute Resolve.
The dialogue continues the progress to rebuild an independent Supreme Court.  The application period for the Supreme Court’s 32 new judges closed November 18 with over 1,300 applicants for these magistrate and other judiciary leadership positions.  The delegations also announced efforts to reform repressive laws, including reform of the Organized Crime and Terrorist Financing Law by the end of this year.  They agreed to conduct a consultation with all political organizations on reforming the Law on Political Parties, focusing on party status, registration updates and revalidation, and the creation of an ombudsman’s office to safeguard political participation.  The two sides also agreed to update and regularize specific broadcast media organizations’ concessions.
We encourage both sides to continue implementing their commitments, ensuring the participation of all political actors, and advancing toward credible elections.  We reiterate our call for the immediate release of all political prisoners.
The Trump Administration remains committed to supporting this Venezuelan-led process as part of President Trump and Secretary Rubio’s three-phase plan for stabilization, economic recovery, and political reconciliation leading to a peaceful democratic transition and an enduring republic.

title: Secretary Rubio’s Call with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Readout


			
			


			
			
November 24, 2026
Secretary Rubio spoke today with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud.  The Secretary condemned the Iran-backed Houthi terrorist attacks on Saudi civilian and energy infrastructure.  The Secretary and the Foreign Minister underscored the necessity of freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab Al-Mandeb.  The two discussed the need to end the war in Sudan, while Secretary Rubio also emphasized the importance of a humanitarian truce, durable peace, and transition to a civilian government. They also discussed the importance of Hizballah’s disarmament in Lebanon under the Trilateral Framework and a shared commitment to regional security and stability.

title: The United States Welcomes the Joint Bid by Chile and Belgium to Host the Secretariat of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement
summary_raw:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
November 24, 2026

The United States welcomes the joint offer by Chile and Belgium to host the Secretariat of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty.  Both countries have a strong record on ocean stewardship and transparency, and their partnership combines complementary expertise and expands diplomatic leadership in a way that reflects the Agreement’s broad membership.  The Trump Administration commends Chilean President Kast and Foreign Minister Pérez Mackenna and Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prevot for their contributions to this initiative.
The BBNJ Agreement can only succeed with a Secretariat that is independent, accountable to BBNJ Parties, and committed to protecting the integrity and security of the data and technology it manages.  If successful, this bid would allow the United States to engage more constructively in the BBNJ Agreement while we assess ratification.  We encourage all Parties to support the Chile-Belgium bid at the first Conference of the Parties in January 2027.
